$comment: Mutation-score floor for the Stryker gate (#74). stryker-config.json's thresholds.break MUST equal 'floor' — Stryker exits non-zero below it, failing the weekly stryker.yaml run, which auto-files an issue. Ratchet policy: the floor only moves UP, in a PR that shows the new sustained score; lowering it requires a written rationale in the same PR. History lives in this file's git log.

measured.environment: GitHub ubuntu-latest, stryker.yaml workflow_dispatch on test/kill-stryker-survivors (run 36266649000), dotnet-stryker from .config/dotnet-tools.json, Release unit suite (408 tests)
measured.note: Single CI run. A local win-x64 run of the same commit reported 93.79 % but with 38 timeouts on an overloaded machine (each scored as a kill), so it was not used; killed counts agree within 1 of the prediction (542 + 27 targeted).

history.note: first real run (stryker.yaml had been a config-less no-op)

#176 pass: 18 behavioural killing tests (verify/recurse flags, exit codes, retention dir + boundary, report counts, filter order, sink defaults) + ignore-methods for Log*/WriteLine* — log-statement mutants are unassertable by design, excluding them turns the score into signal

#176 second pass after the v0.3.0 features dropped the score to 81.12 (below the 83 gate): 27 killing tests - verifier tar-walk isolation (valid compression wrapping non-tar bytes), ctor null-guards, exact retry-attempt counts, skip-mode continuation, byte-count/OriginalSize sums, uniquifier counter progression, directory-entry extraction, expected-size-zero boundary

#268: added ConfigureAwait to ignore-methods. 81 of the 129 survivors in the pre-change run were the same ConfigureAwait(false)->true flip, equivalent by construction in a console app with no SynchronizationContext - the same reasoning that excluded Log*/WriteLine* on 2026-08-29. NOT a testing gain: the pre-change score was 82.84 %, FOUR points below the 2026-09-02 baseline of 86.84 and under the 85 floor, so v0.4.0 code landed without killing tests. Floor moves 85 -> 88 so that regression cannot hide behind the excluded mutants; 88 rather than 89 because two identical-config runs spread 89.65-90.61 on timeout variance and 89 would flake. The 55-64 genuine survivors are the outstanding work.

#300: 16 new tests + assertions added to 5 existing ones, killing 27 genuine survivors (stderr failure line x6, RetentionService guards + missing-dir early return, SharedOptions --name validation, per-strategy compression level incl. Lz4/Zstd MapLevel, default bundle output dir, zip/tar directory entries, --no-lock, csv report, guard ParamNames). Prompted by #298's new PR gate scoring 88.06 % against the 88 floor. First floor set from a Linux CI run rather than a local Windows one; 91 leaves 1.5 points for the ~1-point timeout variance.

survivorProfile: 43 survivors + 4 no-coverage after #300, mostly equivalent by construction: leaveOpen true->false on decompressor/TarWriter wrappers (13), ThrowIfCancellationRequested inside loops whose awaited calls already observe the token (6), sw.Stop() whose elapsed time is only reported (3), message/log strings (~8), FileFilter `Count > 0` -> `>= 0` (an empty exclude matcher excludes nothing), the gzip trailer `||` -> `&&` (the reader rejects a patched ISIZE first) and the gzip <18-byte guard. Remaining genuine candidates: BundleService root-directory name fallback, SharedOptions.ParseDateTime null early-return, CompressionOptions.Verify default. HTML report: the stryker-report-* artifact on the stryker.yaml run.
